phases.name: Slice 01a - Migrate with my own app password (walking skeleton)

steps.name: Password machinery: edited 0001, SCRAM setter, password-taking migrator
criteria: Migration 0001 creates ledgerops_app with no login and no password, and grants CONNECT on the current database whatever its name
Migrate and MigrateStep take the app password; the role gains login and password only after the last migration file
The password reaches the server only as a client-built SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier, Unicode-normalised
Secret and DSN-derived text never render the password under any formatting or error wrap
Ledgercore, multitenancy, intertenanttransfer, postgres-adapter and http-adapter suites stay green passing app-secret explicitly
scenarios: PF :: TestLiveZeroOneIsPinnedOnceEdited
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-017/022, DDD-27/28/47. Edit 0001 once in place; pin its new sha256 in editedZeroOneChecksum and delete the skip. Signature change is compiler-driven across 7 call sites in 6 files (steps_ledger_test.go reaches it via MigrateFromZero). x/text precis becomes a direct dependency. Contract shapes: verifier builder, Secret, redactor pure-function; role setter bounded-change and takes a verifier only, separate port from SchemaMigrator. Unit tests: deterministic vectors plus rapid properties (redactor output never contains the password).

steps.name: migrate command sets the operator-supplied app password
criteria: Empty database ends at schema version 6; app role logs in with the supplied password and is refused with app-secret
Password read from env or file; exactly one trailing line ending removed (line feed, CRLF, none)
Composed, decomposed and fullwidth forms of one password log in interchangeably
Demo password refused at every observed instant; server statement log never holds the plaintext
Cluster changes only by the new app role and ledger schema; no output contains the password

steps.implementation_notes: ADR-018, DDD-30/31. Subcommand dispatcher and ParseMigrateConfig are pure over an env snapshot; password-file reader pure over an injected ReadFile. Order: schema files, then password step last (Rule A by construction). LEDGEROPS_MIGRATE_DSN and LEDGEROPS_APP_PASSWORD[_FILE] read only in the migrate command file (AST test). 10 scenarios, one behaviour: the supplied password is applied and works. Contract shape: bounded-change, state-delta over the catalog universe.

steps.name: Migrate refuses unusable configuration before any change
criteria: Missing, empty or whitespace password: non-zero exit naming both variables, database untouched, app-secret still refused
Both password sources set: refused naming 'only one', cluster unchanged
Insufficient privilege found by read-only facts plus rolled-back probes before any schema change, naming the privilege
Unreachable database reported with the DSN password redacted

scenarios: M01 :: Migrate refuses without a usable password (3 rows)

steps.implementation_notes: ADR-022, DDD-39/42. PlanMigration is pure (facts + config in, refusal or ordered plan out); FactReader is SELECT-only, PreflightProber is write-capable and always rolled back, separate ports. The M04 privilege outline (5 gaps: cannot create roles, no admin option, no database ownership/grant, no CREATE on public, table owned by another role) is pulled into this slice; it uses a non-superuser fixture. Also table-test every refusal reason and add a probe per driven adapter (structural test).

steps.name: Interrupted migrations: no demo login, dirty state refused
criteria: Run killed between two files: schema at version 3, nothing unfinished, app-secret refused
Re-run after a between-files kill completes and the supplied password works
Run killed during a file: migration flagged unfinished, no partial change, app-secret refused
Re-run on a dirty version refuses naming it and changes nothing; no force option exists

steps.implementation_notes: ADR-017, DDD-29. Dirty-state detector is pure: (version, dirty) in, refusal naming the version out. Premise guarded by the kill-mid-file scenario (one implicit transaction per file). The DSN given to golang-migrate never carries x-multi-statement (test). Unit-level coverage only (no acceptance scenario): dirty detector table tests and the no-force-option check.

steps.name: Image ships migrate; demo stack migrates through it
criteria: Non-root image runs migrate from a world-readable secret file and prepares the database
A secret file unreadable by the image user gives a named error and leaves the cluster unchanged
Dockerfile pins every base by digest, cross-compiles on the build platform, runs as 65532 with no step after the final FROM
Demo compose runs the image's migrate with app-secret and the migrate DSN; app never receives the migrate DSN
make up and the demo CI job still pass

Compose migrate becomes build: . with command [migrate], env LEDGEROPS_MIGRATE_DSN (bootstrap superuser) and LEDGEROPS_APP_PASSWORD=app-secret on migrate only; same image tag for migrate and app; no env_file or YAML anchor shared with app; remove migrate/migrate image and bind mount. Dockerfile: alpine:3.24 digest-pinned, golang stage FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM, GOOS/GOARCH from TARGETOS/TARGETARCH, CA bundle copied from build stage. go build carries -tags console_embed (asserted by M07; inert until slice 05 adds the embed pair).

criteria: First ledgerops database in a cluster accepts any name

Refusal names the remedies, including privileged DROP ROLE when the owning database no longer exists
Migrate against the owning or demo-created database is not refused
Output never contains the password in any of five failure situations

steps.implementation_notes: DDD-41/48, ADR-017. Role claim: create ledgerops_app NOLOGIN with owner-database marker (COMMENT ON ROLE) in its own committed transaction; PlanMigration gains the cluster-rule refusal. The M01 outline is mapped here because its fifth row (cluster already holds another ledgerops database) only turns green with this rule. Contract shape: role claim bounded-change. Unit-level coverage only (no acceptance scenario): every cluster-rule refusal reason and remedy text in PlanMigration table tests.

steps.name: Atomic role claim survives abandoned and concurrent runs
criteria: Two simultaneous first migrations in one cluster: exactly one succeeds, loser refuses with the cluster-rule message, neither dirty
Two simultaneous migrations of the same database end consistent
Abandoned claim refuses a different database
Abandoned claim resumes against its own database

M02 :: A first run abandoned after claiming the role resumes against its own database
M02 :: Two simultaneous first migrations in one cluster cannot both claim the role
M02 :: Two simultaneous migrations of the same database end consistent
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-48. No advisory lock (keys are per-database). Loser of the race gets duplicate-object 42710, re-reads the marker and refuses; a re-run against the marked database resumes. Learning hypothesis: a Go-side check cannot be raced; if two runs both pass, move the claim into a single atomic statement.

steps.implementation_notes: ADR-020, DDD-36/50. Classify is pure: (tag, existing registry tags) to ReleasePlan. Output contract: key=value lines version, tags, prerelease, move_latest, highest_stable, resumed. Only strict semver and latest count as existing versions. All 10 acceptance examples drive the real releaseplan subprocess; the 5 properties are layer-1 rapid tests. Classifier is complete (minor/latest tags) because the plan is data; slice 06 only wires extra tags. Delete the LEDGEROPS_RUN_PENDING skip.

steps.name: release.yml: gated, serial, digest-first build
criteria: Trigger is strict version-tag push only; permissions default read-only; release group serialised, never cancels

steps.implementation_notes: ADR-020, DDD-35/37/49, DEVOPS outline jobs 1-3. Path .github/workflows/release.yml is a public interface. Every uses: by full SHA (pins section), checkout persist-credentials false, tag read through env TAG only. build is amd64 only in this run. These seven structural properties are mapped to the earliest step where release.yml can satisfy them; 04-05 and 04-06 must keep them green. The 'only strict tags' scenario also asserts ci.yml has workflow_call, branches-only push, and workflow-guards and container-acceptance jobs (needs integration), so this step makes those ci.yml edits (the called ci job needs workflow_call anyway); 04-06 completes the rest of ci.yml. Criteria 3 (build skipped on resume) and 5 (classify tolerating the first-run 404) have no acceptance scenario: unit-level coverage only (releaseplan/classifier tests).
